title: Oven Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The main cavity temperature sensor is open or shorted.
fullDescription:
Error F1 indicates the PT500 or PT1000 oven temperature sensor is reporting an invalid resistance. The control cannot regulate the bake element and disables heating to prevent runaway temperature.

The sensor is typically mounted on the back wall of the cavity and is inexpensive to replace.

causes.cause: Sensor connector at the rear loose

fixSteps.title: Unplug the oven
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect from mains or turn off the breaker.

fixSteps.title: Remove the sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Unscrew the sensor from the back wall of the cavity and pull the wiring through.

fixSteps.title: Test resistance
fixSteps.instruction: A PT1000 reads about 1080 ohms at 20C. OL or near zero means replace.

fixSteps.title: Install new sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Fit the new sensor and reconnect the harness.

whenToCallPro: If the sensor tests good, the board sensor input needs professional diagnosis.
videoSearchQuery: Siemens oven F1 sensor error fix

faq.q: Is it safe to keep using the oven?
faq.a: No. Without a valid sensor the element could overheat.

title: Overtemperature Cutout
shortDescription: The cavity temperature exceeded a safe limit.
fullDescription: Error F2 is triggered when the measured cavity temperature exceeds the safety threshold. The most common cause is a welded relay on the main board that keeps the element energised, or a pyrolytic cycle that ran too long.
symptoms: Oven very hot even when off

fixSteps.title: Cut power immediately
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the breaker and allow the oven to cool fully.

fixSteps.title: Check the thermal cutout
fixSteps.instruction: Test the rear-panel thermal fuse for continuity and replace if open.

fixSteps.title: Call service for board
fixSteps.instruction: If the relay is welded, the board must be replaced.

whenToCallPro: Always if the relay is suspected welded — this is a fire risk.
videoSearchQuery: Siemens oven F2 overtemperature error fix

faq.a: Potentially yes. Cut power and investigate before resuming use.

title: Door Lock Motor Fault
shortDescription: The pyrolytic door lock did not reach its target position.
fullDescription: Error F3 appears when the motorised door lock used for pyrolytic self-cleaning does not complete its lock or unlock stroke within the expected time window. Grease residue, a worn micro-gear, or a failed microswitch can all trigger it.

fixSteps.title: Power-cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 10 minutes and restore power.

fixSteps.title: Access the lock
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the top cover of the oven to access the door-lock module.

fixSteps.title: Replace the lock
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the complete motorised lock assembly.

whenToCallPro: If the door is jammed shut with food inside and a hot cavity, call service to release safely.
videoSearchQuery: Siemens oven F3 door lock error fix

faq.q: Can I force the lock open?
faq.a: No. Wait for cooldown and replace the lock motor.

title: Cooling Fan Failure
shortDescription: The tangential cooling fan has stopped.
fullDescription: Error F4 indicates the tangential cooling fan above the cavity is not running. This fan draws air across electronics to prevent overheating and vents steam at the door. The oven disables heating until the fan works again.
symptoms: No fan noise when oven heats

fixSteps.title: Unplug and cool
fixSteps.instruction: Power off and let the oven cool before servicing.

fixSteps.title: Clean vents
fixSteps.instruction: Vacuum dust from the top vent and fan cage.

fixSteps.title: Replace cooling fan
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the top cover, unbolt the tangential fan, and install a new unit.

whenToCallPro: If the capacitor is suspect, a pro can test and replace it safely.
videoSearchQuery: Siemens oven F4 cooling fan error fix

faq.q: Can I use the oven until fixed?
faq.a: No. Running without cooling will damage the electronics.

title: Convection Fan Fault
shortDescription: The rear convection fan is not running.
fullDescription: Error F5 indicates the rear cavity convection fan that circulates hot air during hot-air modes has stopped. Its RPM feedback is missing or the motor is drawing abnormal current.

fixSteps.title: Unplug and access
fixSteps.instruction: Cut power and remove the rear cavity panel.

fixSteps.title: Test the motor
fixSteps.instruction: Spin the fan by hand and measure winding resistance.

fixSteps.title: Replace the motor
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new convection motor and reinstall the rear panel.

whenToCallPro: If wiring is melted, call a pro to assess the harness safely.
videoSearchQuery: Siemens oven F5 convection fan error fix

faq.a: On some models yes, with reduced even-heating; on others the oven locks out heating entirely.

title: Convection Element Fault
shortDescription: The ring element behind the rear cover is not heating.
fullDescription: Error F10 indicates the ring convection heating element is open or not drawing current. Hot-air cooking will not reach temperature and the control aborts the program.

fixSteps.title: Unplug the oven
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the breaker.

fixSteps.title: Remove rear cavity panel
fixSteps.instruction: Unscrew the panel to expose the convection element.

fixSteps.title: Test and replace
fixSteps.instruction: Measure element resistance; if open, install a new ring element.

whenToCallPro: If the element is good, the relay on the board is suspect.
videoSearchQuery: Siemens oven F10 convection element error fix

faq.a: Yes if the main bake element is independent and working.

title: Bake Element Fault
shortDescription: The lower bake element is not heating.
fullDescription: Error F11 indicates the bottom bake element is open or its relay is not closing. The cavity does not reach temperature in bake mode and the control halts the cycle.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect power
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the breaker.

fixSteps.title: Remove the element
fixSteps.instruction: Pull out racks, lift the cavity floor if removable, and unscrew the element bracket.

fixSteps.title: Test and replace
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance; install a new element if open.

whenToCallPro: If the relay is at fault, the main board must be replaced.
videoSearchQuery: Siemens oven F11 bake element error fix

faq.q: Why does the element glow red then stop?
faq.a: Often a partial break that opens when hot. Test cold and hot if possible.

title: Grill Element Fault
shortDescription: The top grill element is not heating.
fullDescription: Error F21 indicates the grill element at the top of the cavity is open or its relay failed. Grill and full-grill modes will not operate.

fixSteps.title: Power off
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect breaker and cool the oven.

fixSteps.title: Drop the element
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the screws holding the top element and pull it forward to expose the terminals.

fixSteps.title: Test and replace
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance; swap with a new grill element if open.

whenToCallPro: If the element tests good, a pro should replace the board.
videoSearchQuery: Siemens oven F21 grill element error fix

faq.q: Can I cook without the grill?
faq.a: Yes, bake and convection remain available.

title: Pyrolytic Cycle Aborted
shortDescription: The self-cleaning pyrolytic cycle did not complete.
fullDescription: Error F22 indicates the pyrolytic cleaning cycle aborted due to overtemperature, door-lock failure, or a door that was opened during cleaning.

fixSteps.title: Let it cool
fixSteps.instruction: Allow the oven to cool until the door unlocks automatically.

fixSteps.title: Remove loose debris
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe out burned residue and heavy grease before rerunning the cycle.

fixSteps.title: Diagnose lock
fixSteps.instruction: If F22 recurs with door-lock issues, refer to F3 service steps.

whenToCallPro: If the overtemperature cutout tripped, a pro should verify the cavity and relay are safe.
videoSearchQuery: Siemens oven F22 pyrolytic error fix

faq.q: Should I run pyro with lots of grease?
faq.a: No. Remove heavy soil first to avoid smoke and overtemperature trips.

title: Display Communication Error
shortDescription: The TFT display has lost communication with the main board.
fullDescription: Error F31 indicates the TFT / LCD display controller is not communicating with the main control board. The display may go blank or show the error persistently.

fixSteps.title: Power-cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for five minutes.

fixSteps.title: Reseat ribbon
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the control panel and reseat the display ribbon at both ends.

fixSteps.title: Replace display
fixSteps.instruction: If the module is dead, install a new TFT display module.

whenToCallPro: TFT replacements are expensive — confirm diagnosis with a pro before ordering the part.
videoSearchQuery: Siemens oven F31 display error fix

faq.q: Is it safe to use the oven?
faq.a: No. Without reliable display feedback, you cannot confirm temperature.

title: EEPROM / Memory Error
shortDescription: The control board cannot read its stored configuration.
fullDescription: Error F32 indicates the non-volatile memory on the main control board has failed or has been corrupted, possibly by a power surge. The board cannot read calibration and disables cooking.

fixSteps.title: Power-cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 15 minutes to attempt a soft recovery.

fixSteps.title: Call service
fixSteps.instruction: If F32 persists, the main board must be replaced or reprogrammed.

videoSearchQuery: Siemens oven F32 EEPROM error fix

faq.q: Can I reset the EEPROM myself?
faq.a: Generally no. The board requires a service programmer.

title: Relay Mismatch
shortDescription: A relay did not switch as commanded.
fullDescription: Error F42 indicates the board commanded a heating relay to open or close, but the current-sense feedback did not match. This can mean a welded relay, a failed driver transistor, or a shorted element keeping the relay energised.
symptoms: Heating does not start when commanded

fixSteps.title: Disconnect power
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the breaker — F42 can indicate a runaway relay.

fixSteps.title: Call service
fixSteps.instruction: Have a technician check all elements and the board.

whenToCallPro: Always. F42 is a safety-critical fault that may indicate a runaway relay.
videoSearchQuery: Siemens oven F42 relay error fix
